title: Pilot 2 — Independent Model Perspectives
description:
Pilot 2 is the next bounded implementation step after Pilot 1.

It asks two genuinely independent model families to analyze the same synthetic or publication-safe evidence packet without seeing each other's first-pass output, validates both outputs deterministically, and preserves agreement and disagreement without treating consensus as truth.

Pilot 2 does not introduce private Session Search intake or canonical-memory writes.

Pilot 2 is the next bounded implementation step after Pilot 1.

It asks two genuinely independent model families to analyze the same synthetic or publication-safe evidence packet without seeing each other's first-pass output, validates both outputs deterministically, and preserves agreement and disagreement without treating consensus as truth.

Pilot 2 does not introduce private Session Search intake or canonical-memory writes.

rules.requirement: The two first passes are genuinely independent
rules:
The two configured routes MUST declare different model-family identities.

Two provider endpoints declaring the same base model family MUST NOT satisfy this requirement.

The first bounded orchestrator proves only `CONFIGURED_DISTINCT`: it rejects equal configured family identities before inference and preserves observed provider/model metadata from each pass. Stronger transport-level family verification belongs to the provider adapter. If route identity is invalid or configured independence cannot be established, Pilot 2 MUST return `FAIL_CLOSED` rather than claiming two independent perspectives.

Pass A MUST NOT receive Pass B output before completing.

Pass B MUST NOT receive Pass A output before completing.

Any optional critique/conclave phase MAY start only after both first-pass artifacts are frozen.

rules.requirement: Both passes see the same primary evidence
rules:
Both first passes MUST receive the same evidence packet, evidence fingerprint, task, coverage/currentness state, and safe scope.

Per-provider prompt wrappers MAY differ only where required by the provider adapter; they MUST NOT alter the semantic evidence set.

rules.requirement: Each pass uses the Pilot 1 proposal contract
rules:
Each successful pass MUST produce a valid `theseus.dreaming-worker.proposals.v1` proposal set.

Each pass MUST independently pass schema and exact-provenance validation.

A malformed or provenance-invalid pass is a typed failure, not a valid perspective.

rules.requirement: Terminal state distinguishes absence from analysis failure
Pass failure and receipt uncertainty stay explicit

rules:
Comparison MUST be based on already-frozen validated first-pass records.

The first bounded implementation MUST compare exact structured proposal fingerprints deterministically and preserve pass-specific proposals. It MUST leave semantic relation explicitly unresolved rather than pretending to detect contradiction from free-form claims.

The comparison layer MUST NOT collapse disagreement into a consensus score or majority-vote truth.

Pilot 2 MAY support a later critique/conclave pass, but the first implementation MUST NOT require it.

If critique is added, it MUST receive references to frozen first-pass artifacts and MUST remain a derived proposal, not an acceptance authority.

Pilot 2 MUST NOT widen data egress beyond the scopes already accepted for Pilot 1.

Private or unclassified Session Search evidence remains outside Pilot 2 until a separate source-reader and egress authorization is verified.
If Pilot 0 returns `NO_DATA`, Pilot 2 MUST make zero external model calls.

A separate pure pool selector MAY choose the routes for two independent first-pass slots, or the one missing slot if an independently validated perspective is already frozen. It MUST use explicit caller-supplied free research admission, current catalog presence, task qualification, finite remaining attempt budget, prior attempted route identities, and known route/provider cooldowns. Catalog presence alone MUST NOT establish permission or quality. Unknown entitlement or stale/unknown catalog MUST NOT be eligible.

A ready selection MUST contain only unattempted, eligible, currently ready routes of distinct configured model families, also distinct from the frozen perspective family. A frozen perspective MUST NOT be invalidated solely because its old route retires. Prefer different configured provider domains among ready choices, then deterministic rotation. An unresolved earlier attempt MUST block selection.

When an eligible independent selection exists only after cooldown, report its earliest feasible wake time (all required slots must be feasible before catalog evidence expires). Revalidate on wake. Insufficient eligibility or budget is not NO_DATA. The selector MUST NOT invoke inference, reserve work, infer entitlement, establish semantic quality or advance a checkpoint. Integration with durable recovery requires separate acceptance; existing fixed-pair execution is unchanged.

scenarios.requirement: The two first passes are genuinely independent
scenarios.name: Distinct model families are accepted
given: two approved routes with different model-family identities
then: the independent two-pass run may proceed

scenarios.requirement: The two first passes are genuinely independent
scenarios.name: Same model family through two routes is rejected
given: two routes that resolve to the same model family
then: outcome is FAIL_CLOSED
AND neither provider pass is invoked

scenarios.name: Passes run before comparison
given: one evidence packet and two approved independent routes
when: Pass A and Pass B execute
then: neither first-pass input contains the other pass's proposal output
AND comparison begins only after both first-pass records are frozen or one pass has terminated with a typed failure

scenarios.requirement: Both passes see the same primary evidence
scenarios.name: Exact evidence parity
given: one accepted evidence packet
then: both invocations record the same evidence fingerprint
AND the same request/task fingerprint
AND the same coverage/currentness state

scenarios.requirement: Each pass uses the Pilot 1 proposal contract
scenarios.name: Pass B invents a source reference
given: Pass A returns valid proposals
AND Pass B returns a proposal with an invented source reference or wrong evidence hash
then: Pass B becomes a typed invalid-output failure
AND its proposal is not admitted as a valid perspective

scenarios.requirement: Terminal state distinguishes absence from analysis failure
scenarios.name: Both providers fail after evidence was accepted
given: Pilot 0 accepted evidence
AND both configured-distinct first passes terminate with typed failures
then: outcome is FAIL_CLOSED
AND outcome is not NO_DATA
AND both typed failures remain visible

scenarios.requirement: Terminal state distinguishes absence from analysis failure
scenarios.name: Configured independence is not established
given: Pilot 0 accepted evidence
AND both routes declare the same model family
then: outcome is FAIL_CLOSED
AND external model calls equal zero

scenarios.requirement: Pass failure and receipt uncertainty stay explicit
scenarios.name: Provider times out after inference was invoked
given: one pass succeeds
AND the other invoked pass terminates with a timeout whose provider-side completion state is unknown
then: the failed pass is TIMEOUT_UNKNOWN_PROVIDER_STATE
AND the successful pass contributes to confirmedExternalModelCalls
AND the failed invoked pass contributes to unresolvedExternalCallAttempts

scenarios.requirement: Pass failure and receipt uncertainty stay explicit
scenarios.name: Output budget is exhausted before final content
given: a provider returns empty final content with finish reason length
then: the pass failure is OUTPUT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED

scenarios.requirement: Pass failure and receipt uncertainty stay explicit
scenarios.name: Transport rejects structured JSON generation
given: a provider adapter reports json_validate_failed
then: the pass failure is JSON_VALIDATE_FAILED

scenarios.requirement: Pass failure and receipt uncertainty stay explicit
scenarios.name: Returned provider metadata survives later validation failure
given: a provider returns observed provider/model metadata and model output
AND the returned output later fails JSON, schema, provenance, or policy validation
then: configured route identity remains visible
AND observed provider/model metadata remains separately visible
AND the failed pass does not contribute to confirmedExternalModelCalls

scenarios.name: One provider times out
given: Pass A succeeds
AND Pass B times out
then: outcome is PARTIAL
AND Pass A remains available
AND Pass B timeout remains visible
AND no substitute provider is silently invoked

scenarios.name: Models produce different hypotheses
given: two valid first-pass proposal sets with one exact structured match and pass-specific proposals
then: both original proposal sets remain intact
AND the exact match is represented by a shared proposal fingerprint
AND pass-specific proposals remain separately fingerprinted
AND semantic relation is UNRESOLVED_WITHOUT_CRITIQUE
AND no consensus truth classification is emitted

scenarios.name: First implementation has no critic
given: two valid first-pass outputs
when: Pilot 2 completes without a critique model
then: the result is still valid
AND the comparison artifact remains descriptive rather than authoritative

scenarios.name: Private scope is requested
given: a request outside SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE and PUBLICATION_SAFE
then: no provider call is made

scenarios.name: Pilot 0 returns NO_DATA
given: no accepted new evidence
then: external model calls equal zero
AND outcome is NO_DATA

scenarios.name: Retirement and bounded replacement
given: explicitly admitted task-qualified routes of distinct families and one frozen perspective
when: a route retires or a known failure excludes an attempted route
then: only the missing slot is selected from other eligible families
AND unknown prior execution blocks any selection

scenarios.name: Feasible wake and independent pair
given: known provider and route cooldowns and expiring catalog observations
then: deferral is only to the earliest time a full independent selection can be feasible
AND stale admission, exhausted budget or insufficient families cannot be converted into readiness
